Please Be Careful With Your Pets Here!!!

I am writing this review because I do not want another family to experience what happened to my beloved cat.

My cat was taken to this veterinary practice and was diagnosed with cancer by Dr. Ivanov. My cat never had cancer. We later learned that the diagnosis was incorrect, yet she was prescribed medication based on that diagnosis. My cat was was given Felanorm.
After starting the medication, my cat became extremely lethargic. I specifically contacted the veterinarian and told him that my cat was becoming lethargic after taking the medication. Instead of telling me to stop the medication, bring her back to the hospital, or have her urgently evaluated, I was told to continue giving it to her.

I trusted the veterinarian because I believed he knew what was best for my cat. I followed the medical instructions I was given, and we ultimately lost my cat. From my perspective, I was put in an impossible position: I reported that my cat was becoming seriously lethargic, I trusted the veterinarian’s instructions, and I was told to continue the medication. I will live with the guilt and heartbreak of that decision for the rest of my life. I truly believe continuing this medication after I reported her worsening condition contributed to her death.

My cat was a beloved member of our family. We trusted this veterinarian to properly diagnose her and treat her safely, and instead, we lost her. We are devastated and feel that we were failed when our cat needed proper medical care the most.

What makes this even more concerning is that I have found other pet owners reporting serious problems involving their cats and this same medication, including reports of cats becoming seriously ill or passing away. I cannot personally verify the circumstances of those cases, but I believe these reports deserve to be investigated and taken seriously.

I am also very concerned by the way this business responds to negative reviews. Some responses to patients come across as aggressive and defensive rather than compassionate. I sincerely hope this review is not met with another defensive response or an attempt to dismiss our experience. Families who lose their pets deserve to be heard, and legitimate concerns about a pet’s diagnosis and treatment deserve answers, not hostility. After our experience, I am left questioning whether the priority was truly my cats health and well-being or whether financial considerations played too large a role in her care. That is how this experience made me feel as a grieving pet owner. Please protect your pets. Ask for copies of all medical records, test results, and treatment notes. Get a second opinion if something does not seem right. Ask detailed questions about every medication prescribed, its potential side effects, and exactly what you should do if your pet’s condition changes or gets worse.

My cat trusted us to protect her, and we trusted this veterinarian to help us protect her. We feel that trust was broken. I will always regret following the instruction to continue a medication after I had already reported that she was becoming lethargic.
My cat deserved better. She was loved, she was part of our family, and she mattered. 💔🐾
I am sharing our experience because I hope it encourages other pet owners to ask questions, get second opinions, obtain their pets’ medical records, and advocate for their animals before it is too late.

My cats life mattered, and our family will never forget her.

I switched to VCG -Middle Village after intensive research looking for my Minkie’s previous vet.  Found her in Oyster Bay which is too far to drive especially in an emergency. She took her time, heard all of our concerns and we worked out a good plan for my pooch and she was now on the right track after several months of illness. A bonus was finding out that Dr. Schwartz worked with Minkie’s previous vet at the Oyster Bay location as well.  Sad to learn Dr. Schwartz has left but we are now working with Dr. Ivanov and received the same quality of care.  To get a check in call at 8:15pm let’s me know we made a good choice.  Comforting to feel like we are all on the same page especially when dealing with a dog with a chronic illness.  The receptionists are great here too.  Minkie is very nervous at the vet since COVID and they take great care of her helping her settle down since we still cannot go inside with her.

A reply to the clinic's response:
Why would you lie now? There wasn't any "treatment plan outlined to manage my cat's comfort at home" - nothing besides what I described in my review - I have her complete medical records right in front of me. No risks of any medications given to my cat were ever discussed either.

This isn't going to be a short review because the list of things that shouldn't have happened is a long one.
I brought my CeCe for a check up because she had been eating poorly, loosing weight and having less energy for a couple of weeks. Before her blood tests results were even known, and confirmed advanced stage of kidney disease, Dr. Ueda had decided to treat my cat with a concoction of an aggressive parasite treatment, and an undisclosed antibiotic - "just in case" - without any symptoms calling for its use. Had I been told about the common side effects of both medications (NexGard Combo and Convenia), I would have never given consent to have either one of them used on my cat. Dr. Ueda failed to obtain an informed consent from me, and under the guise of "making my cat feel better" treated her with two substances that were guaranteed to worsen the very symptoms I came to seek treatment for. Afterwards, when my cat's condition did worsen - she became completely letargic and anorexic - and I couldn't afford the recommended $7000 hospitalization, I asked for home palliative care options. All I was sent away with were subcutaneous fluids, phosphate binder (Epakitin) that was supposed to be given with food, and a transdermal appetite stimulant (Mirataz) that the vet herself admitted wouldn't work. Neither nausea nor pain medication were prescribed, which essentially meant my non-eating cat was left to starve to death. She couldn't eat because the uremic toxins in her body caused extreme nausea and painful ulcers. Yet, at first, I was told she couldn't be nauseous because she wasn't actively vomiting. My request for a pain medication was also denied supposedly because Dr. Ueda didn't notice any ulcers - how could she though, if she never even finished checking my cat's mouth. Later on I was told that these safe liver-metabolized medications (like Cerenia or Buprenorphine), commonly prescribed to cats with kidney disease, couldn't be given to my cat because they would "further strain her compromized kidneys." And that was not only a blatant lie, but it also made for a most ridiculous excuse since two harsh systemic medications that are specifically kidney-metabolized had been administered or dispensed to my cat just a few days prior, without blinking an eye. In reply to my final plea for a pain medication to ease my dying CeCe's suffering, l was rushed (because they were closing soon) to bring her in for a euthanasia estimated at $500-700 even though I explained she was in no condition to be moved. No other options were offered or suggested.
Nobody who truly loves animals would have done or let any of this happen. Stay away from this place. These "nice people" are only after your money.
